headline: Fail-closed robustness for malformed certificates and truncated encrypted blobs
summary: Three robustness fixes on the certificate, crypto-envelope, and backup-lock paths so a malformed input fails cleanly instead of crashing or leaking a raw library error.

items.title: Certificate fingerprinting no longer crashes on a malformed certificate
items.body: A certificate whose PEM body is non-empty but base64-decodes to zero bytes produced an empty re-encoding, and the line-wrapping step then threw a TypeError on the certificate-fingerprint / revocation path. It now yields a stable empty canonical form — which hashes deterministically and simply never matches a revocation entry — instead of throwing.

items.title: A truncated legacy encrypted blob fails with the typed envelope error
items.body: The legacy-format decrypt path had a dead length check that could never fire, so a blob whose ciphertext was shorter than the required 16-byte authentication tag fell through to a raw cipher-library error instead of the framework's typed 'Invalid envelope' error. The check now enforces the minimum tag length and fails closed with the typed error.

items.title: The backup/restore operation lock releases even if start-audit logging fails
items.body: The 'operation started' audit emit for a backup or restore now runs inside the lock's try/finally region, so the in-progress lock is released unconditionally — a start-audit failure can no longer leave the lock latched and wedge every subsequent backup and restore until a restart.
